stem: A client has dysphagia and a decreased level of consciousness. Which pulmonary complication is this client at increased risk for?

options.C: Pulmonary embolism caused by impaired swallowing

rationale: NCBI clinical references identify both impaired swallowing and impaired consciousness as important aspiration-risk factors. Failure of normal airway-protective mechanisms allows oropharyngeal secretions or gastric contents to enter the lower respiratory tract, which can lead to aspiration pneumonia.
educational_objective: Recognize dysphagia and reduced consciousness as major risk factors for aspiration and aspiration pneumonia.
source_version_date: Aspiration Pneumonia updated 2024-03-20; Aspiration Risk current 2026
source_locator: Aspiration Pneumonia > Etiology and History and Physical; Aspiration Risk > risk factors and airway protection
source_claim_supported: Dysphagia and altered or impaired consciousness increase aspiration risk by impairing swallowing and airway-protective mechanisms and can lead to aspiration pneumonia.
correction_summary: Removed the family-member framing and cue-heavy explanatory distractors. Retained the supported clinical relationship between dysphagia, decreased consciousness, aspiration, and aspiration pneumonia.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by the identified risk factors. B and C are not caused by dysphagia/decreased consciousness through this mechanism, and D is an unsupported pathogen-specific conclusion. No second answer remains.
